chapter: First bands and New Orleans style
title: Harmony playing, favorite clarinetists, Bechet and the Young Olympia band
summary: He played lead and second harmony; admired Bechet and Edmund Hall; recalls Bechet in the Young Olympia band with Buddy Petit, Armstrong and Marrero.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: You were, in your style of music now you play a lot of harmony parts on the clarinet. Did you always play like that? You know what I mean? You play, your style of music you play a lot of harmony parts in the other couple of choruses, you played other harmonies to the lead. Did you always play that play?
Yes, but I played the lead also. But I do that when the trumpet is playing, and I play a second of the harmony. But I play both the lead and the big harmony. Yeah. I call it the second.
Yeah. What saxophone or clarinet players were there around in the early days, besides Sidney Bechet, which you liked to listen to? Who else was there, you know, that you liked to listen to?

Well there wasn't anyone outside of Sidney Bechet on the saxophone, but now the clarinet players around, after Sidney then left was Hall. I forget Hall's name, he played a thing with Louis Young, so he passed away. Edmund Hall? Edmund Hall, he was a very good clarinet player, I liked him very much. I always liked the Rinder Theo's clarinet player very much. But Sidney Bechet, he was chief.
What bands did you hear Sidney work with? I mean, who was he playing with at this time, Sidney Bechet?

At the time before Sidney left, he was playing with a band, they called himself, the Young Olympia band. And that was with Siren Moreira, and Buddy P.T. Sometimes Buddy would send Louis Armstrong into his place, and John Marrero. They had a wonderful band. Yeah.
